description:
If you own a flat, there is one number in your sale deed worth finding tonight.

A flat does not come with its own plot. It comes with an "undivided share of land", a portion of the land under the building that all owners hold together. In one published example, 200 flats stand on 40,000 sq ft of land, so a 1,000 sq ft flat owns about 228 sq ft of it. Families who prefer a plot like owning the whole piece of land; families who prefer a flat value security, lifts and a home that is ready. If an old building is ever rebuilt, this share is what your new home is worked out from.

In your family, who wants the plot and who wants the flat?

(Worked example from Housing.com; the share varies by project. Sources: Housing.com, Brigade Group, BankBazaar. Some scenes are AI visualisation. For education only.)
